stemMd: Why is a pollen percentage not a simple census of nearby plants?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Plants differ in pollen output, and pollen can arrive from different distances.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Lakes preserve pollen only from insect-pollinated plants.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Researchers count leaves instead of identifying pollen.

options.label: D
options.textMd: All deeper sediment layers formed more recently than upper layers.

explanationMd: The second paragraph names two biases: unequal pollen production and unequal transport distances. Either prevents a direct conversion from pollen percentage to local plant abundance.

distractorRationale.c: The research uses both types of evidence.
distractorRationale.b: The passage explains that abundant wind-carried pollen can be preserved.
distractorRationale.d: The stated usual sequence is the reverse.
